faculty.lab: Not separately named; personal group + HAVA Lab (co-PI with Cees Snoek) and AI4Film; hyperbolic-geometry research programme.
faculty.research_areas: Hyperbolic deep learning: hierarchical and structured representation learning, vision-language models, out-of-distribution robustness, zero-shot learning - all built on the premise that hierarchies are geometrically hyperbolic, not Euclidean.
faculty.why_match: HiME's entire claim is that hierarchy consistency should be guaranteed BY CONSTRUCTION rather than repaired post hoc - chain-rule decoding of per-level conditional sigmoids yields an upward-closed prediction set as a theorem, at ~0.01% parameter overhead, verified on Galaxy Zoo 2's 4-level/37-class taxonomy. Mettes's entire hyperbolic-learning programme makes the identical structural argument at the level of the embedding SPACE rather than the decoding rule: his own research statement, VERBATIM, is 'hierarchies are hyperbolic in nature due to their exponential growth... Euclidean geometry however has critical blindspots.' 'Designing Hierarchies for Optimal Hyperbolic Embedding' (ESWC 2025, best-paper nomination) and 'Hyperbolic Learning with Supervision from any Granularity' (AISTATS 2026) directly ask HiME's question - how to encode a multi-level taxonomy so that consistency is geometrically free - and 'Hyperbolic Part-Whole Image Segmentation' (AISTATS 2026) is a segmentation-flavoured version of the same idea. His 'Balanced Hyperbolic Embeddings Are Natural Out-of-Distribution Detectors' (IJCV 2026) also speaks to Akshat's DDPM negative result (liver works, kidney fails) - a geometry-first account of when a learned representation transfers and when it doesn't.
faculty.key_paper_1: Designing Hierarchies for Optimal Hyperbolic Embedding. ESWC, 2025 (best paper nomination).
faculty.key_paper_2: Hyperbolic Learning with Supervision from any Granularity. AISTATS, 2026. (See also: Hyperbolic Deep Learning in Computer Vision: A Survey, IJCV 2024; Balanced Hyperbolic Embeddings Are Natural Out-of-Distribution Detectors, IJCV 2026.)

faculty.lab: AMLab; geometric/equivariant deep learning programme, part of 'ideal-machine-intelligence.eu' collaboration.
faculty.research_areas: Geometric deep learning: group-equivariant CNNs on Lie groups, steerable/B-spline convolutions, hierarchical tree-based transformers for large physical systems, equivariant generative models (flow matching), discrete-structure representations.
faculty.why_match: HiME is a 'guarantee by construction' architecture: hierarchy consistency is a theorem baked into the decoding rule, not something learned or corrected after the fact. Bekkers's foundational work is the same design philosophy applied to a different symmetry group: 'B-Spline CNNs on Lie Groups' (ICLR 2019) builds equivariance directly into the convolution kernel, and his 2025-2026 AMLab output pushes the SAME idea toward hierarchy specifically - 'Erwin: A Tree-based Hierarchical Transformer for Large-scale Physical Systems' (ICML 2025, with Welling and van de Meent) uses ball-tree partitioning and progressive coarsening/refinement to build a genuinely hierarchical attention mechanism, and 'CORDS: Continuous Representations of Discrete Structures' (ICLR 2026) is directly about representing discrete/hierarchical structure in a continuous, differentiable way - conceptually adjacent to HiME's per-level conditional sigmoid decoding.

As AMLab director he sits at the centre of exactly the generative-modeling ecosystem (QUVA/Delta/AI4Science labs) the target description invokes.
